verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिर उवाच। तस्मिन्नन्तर्हिते विप्रे राजा किमकरोत्तदा । भार्या चास्य महाभागा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said After the Rishi had disappeared, what did the king do and what also his highly-blessed wife? Tell me this O grandfather.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच। अदृष्ट्वा स महीपालस्तमृषिं सह भार्यया । परिश्रान्तो निववृते व्रीडितो नष्टचेतनः ॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Not seeing the Rishi, the king, Stricken with shame, toilworn, and losing his senses, returned to his palace, accompanied by his queen.

verses.sanskrit: स प्रविश्य पुरीं दीनो नाभ्यभाषत किञ्चन । तदेव चिन्तयामास च्यवनस्य विचेष्टितम् ॥३॥
verses.english: Entering his mansion in a dejected spirit, The spoke not a word with any one. He thought only of that conduct of Chyavana.

verses.sanskrit: अथ शून्येन मनसा प्रविश्य स्वगृहं नृपः । ददर्श शयने तस्मिन् शयानं भृगुनन्दनम् ॥४॥
verses.english: With a despairing heart he then went to his room. There he beheld the son of Bhrigu stretched as before on his bed.

verses.sanskrit: विस्मितौ तमृषिं दृष्ट्वा तदाश्चर्यं विचिन्त्य च । दर्शनात्तस्य तु तदा विश्रान्तौ सम्बभूवतुः॥५॥
verses.english: Seeing the Rishi there, they wondered much. Indeed, they began to think upon that very strange incident. The sight of the Rishi removed their fatigue.

verses.sanskrit: यथास्थानं च तौ स्थित्वा भूयस्तं संववाहतुः । अथापरेण पार्श्वेन सुष्वाप स महामुनिः ॥६॥
verses.english: Seated once more by his side, they again began to gently press his feet as before. Meanwhile the great ascetic continued to sleep soundly as before. Only, he now lay on another side.

verses.sanskrit: तेनैव च स कालेन प्रत्यबुद्ध्यत वीर्यवान् । न च तौ चक्रतुः किञ्चिद्विकारं भयशङ्कितौ ॥७॥
verses.english: Gifted with great energy, he thus passed another twentyone days. Moved by fear, the royal pair showed no change in their attitude or sentiment towards the Rishi.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिबुद्धस्तु स मुनिस्तौ प्रोवाच विशाम्पते । तैलाभ्यङ्गो दीयतां मे स्नास्येऽहमिति भारत ॥८॥
verses.english: Awaking then from his sleep the ascetic addressed the king and the queen, saying-do you rub my body with oil, I wish to have a bath.

verses.sanskrit: तौ तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य क्षुधितौ श्रमकर्शितौ । शतपाकेन तैलेन महार्हेणोपतस्थतुः ॥९॥
verses.english: Famishing and toilworn though they were, forthwith they volunteered their services and soon approached the Rishi with a rich oil that had been prepared by boiling it a hundred times.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सुखासीनमृषिं वाग्यतौ संववाहतुः । न च पर्याप्तमित्याह भार्गवः सुमहातपाः ॥१०॥
verses.english: While the Rishi was seated at his ease, the king and the queen, silently, continued to rub him. Gifted with great ascetic merit, the son of Bhrigu did not once utter the word Sufficient.

verses.sanskrit: यदा तौ निर्विकारौ तु लक्षयामास भार्गवः । तत उत्थाय सहसा स्नानशालां विवेश ह ॥११॥
verses.english: Bhrigu's son however saw that the royal pair were totally unmoved. Rising up all on a sudden, he entered the bath room.

verses.sanskrit: क्लृप्तमेव तु तत्रासीत्स्नानीयं पार्थिवोचितम् । असत्कृत्य च तत्सर्वं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥१२॥
verses.english: The various articles necessary for a bath and such as were fit for a king's use, were ready there. Without using, any of those articles, the Rishi once more disappeared there and then by his Yogapower, before king Kushika (and his wife). This, however, O chief of Bharatas, failed to disturb the equanimity of the royal pair.

verses.sanskrit: स मुनिः पुनरेवाथ नृपतेः पश्यतस्तदा । नासूयां चक्रतुस्तौ च दम्पती भरतर्षभ ॥१३॥
अथ स्नातः स भगवान्सिंहासनगतः प्रभुः । दर्शयामास कुशिकं सभार्यं कुरुनन्दन ॥१४॥
verses.english: The next time the powerful Rishi was seen seated, after a bath, on the throne. It was from that place that he then showed himself to the king and the queen, O delighter of the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: संहृष्टवद‌नो राजा सभार्यः कुशिको मुनिम् । सिद्धमन्नमिति प्रह्वो निर्विकारो न्यवेदयत् ॥१५॥
verses.english: With a cheerful face, king Kushika, together with his wife, then offered the Rishi cooked food with great respect. Gifted with wisdom, and with heart totally unmoved, Kushika made this offer.

verses.sanskrit: आनीयतामिति मुनिस्तं चोवाच नराधिपम् । स राजा समुपाजह्रे तदन्नं सह भार्यया ॥१६॥
verses.english: The Ascetic said Let the food be brought. Assisted by his wife, the king soon brought there the food.

verses.sanskrit: मांसप्रकारान्विविधान् शाकानि विविधानि च । वेसवारविकारांश्च पानकानि लघूनि च ॥१७॥
verses.english: There were various kinds of meat and different preparations also thereof. There was a great variety of vegetables also and potherbs.

verses.sanskrit: रसालापूपकांश्चित्रान्मोदकानथ खाण्डवान् । रसान्नानाप्रकारांश्च वन्यं च मुनिभोजनम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: There were juicy cakes too among those dishes and several agreeable kinds of confectionery, and solid preparations of milk. Indeed, the viands were different in kinds and taste. Among them there were also some foodforest produces-such as ascetics liked and took.

verses.sanskrit: फलानि च विचित्राणि राजभोज्यानि भूरिशः। बदरेङ्गुद‌काश्मर्यभल्लातकफलानि च ॥१९॥
verses.english: Various sweet fruits fit to be eaten by kings, were also there. There were Vadaras and Ingudas and Kahsmaryyas and Bhallatakas.

verses.sanskrit: गृहस्थानां च यद्भोज्यं यच्चापि वनवासिनाम् । सर्वमाहारयामास राजा शापभयात्ततः ॥२०॥
verses.english: The food that was offered contained such things as are taken by householders, as also such things as arc taken by the forest dwellers. Through fear of the Rishi's curse, the king had caused all kinds of food to be gathered and got ready for his guest.

verses.sanskrit: अथ सर्वमुपन्यस्तमग्रतश्च्यवनस्य तत् । ततः सर्वं समानीय तच्च शय्यासनं मुनिः ॥२१॥
verses.english: All this food, brought from the kitchen, was placed before Chyavana. A seat was also placed for him and a bed too was spread. The dishes were then caused to be covered with white cloths. Soon, however, Chyavana of Bhrigu's race put fire to all the things and reduced them to ashes.

verses.sanskrit: वस्त्रैः शुभैरवच्छाद्य भोजनोपस्करैः सह । सर्वमादीपयामास च्यवनो भृगुनन्दनः ॥२२॥
न च तौ चक्रतुः क्रोधं दम्पती सुमहामती । तयोः संप्रेक्षतोरेव पुनरन्तर्हितोऽभवत् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Gifted with great intelligence, the royal pair showed no anger at this conduct of the Rishi, who once more, after this, disappeared before the very eyes of the king and the queen.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव च स राजर्षिस्तस्थौ तां रजनीं तदा । सभार्यो वाग्यतः श्रीमान्न च कोपं समाविशद ॥२४॥
verses.english: The royal sage Kushika thereupon stood there in the same posture for the whole night, with his wife by his side, and without speaking a word. Gifted with great prosperity, he did not yield to wrath.

verses.sanskrit: नित्यसंस्कृतमन्नं तु विविधं राजवेश्मनि । शयनानि च मुख्यानि परिषेकाश्च पुष्कलाः ॥२५॥
verses.english: Every day, good and pure food of various sorts, excellent beds, profuse articles needed for bath, and cloths of various sorts, were collected and kept ready in the palace for the Rishi. Indeed, Chyavana could not find any fault in the conduct of the king.

verses.sanskrit: वस्त्रं च विविधाकारमभवत्समुपार्जितम् । न शशाक ततो द्रष्टुमन्तरं च्यवनस्तदा ॥२६॥
पुनरेव च विप्रर्षिः प्रोवाच कुशिकं नृपम् । सभार्यो मां रथेनाशु वह यत्र ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Then addressing king Kushika, the twice born Rishi said to him, “Do you with your spouse, yoke yourself to a car and take me on it wherever I shall direct."

verses.sanskrit: तथेति च प्राह नृपो निर्विशङ्कस्तपोधनम् । क्रीडारथोऽस्तु भगवन्नुत सांग्रामिको रथः ॥२८॥
verses.english: Unhesitatingly, the king answered Chyavana having asceticism for wealth, saying-So be it! And he further enquired of the Rishi, asking-Which car shall I bring? Shall it be my pleasure car for making pleasure journeys or, shall it be my war-chariot?

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तः स मुनी राज्ञा तेन हृष्टेन तद्वचः । च्यवनः प्रत्युवाचेदं हृष्टः परपुरञ्जयम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by the delighted and contented King, the ascetic said to him-Do you promptly get ready that chariot with which you attack hostile cities! cities! Indeed, that warchariot of yours, with every weapon, with its standard and flags, its darts and javelins and golden columns and poles, should be made ready. Its rattle resembles the tinkling of bells. It is adorned with numberless arches made of pure gold. It is always furnished with hundreds of high and excellent weapons!

verses.sanskrit: सज्जीकुरु रथं क्षिप्रं यस्ते सांग्रामिको मतः । सायुधः सपताकश्च शक्तीकनकयष्टिमान् ॥३०॥
किङ्किणीस्वननिर्घोषो युक्तस्तोरणकल्पनैः । जाम्बूनद‌निबद्धश्च परमेषुशतान्वितः ॥३१॥
ततः स तं तथेत्युक्त्वा कल्पयित्वा महारथम् । भार्यां वामे धुरि तदा चात्मानं दक्षिणे तथा ॥३२॥
verses.english: The king said So be it, and soon made his great warchariot ready. And he yoked his wife thereto on the left and his own self on the right, And the king placed on the chariot, among its other articles, the goad which had three handles and which had a point hard as adamant and sharp as the needle.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिदण्डं वज्रसूच्यग्रं प्रतोदं तत्र चादधत् । सर्वमेतत्तथा दत्वा नृपो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ॥३३॥
भगवन्क्व रथो यातु ब्रवीतु भृगुनन्दन । यत्र वक्ष्यसि विप्रर्षे तत्र यास्यति ते रथः ॥३४॥
verses.english: Having placed every article upon the car, the king said to the Rishi-O holy one, where shall the chariot proceed? O let the son of Bhrigu issue his order.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान्प्रत्युवाचाथ तं नृपम् । इतः प्रभृति यातव्यं पदकं पदकं शनैः ॥३५॥
verses.english: This your chariot shall proceed to the place which you may be pleased to direct! Thus addressed, the holy' man replied to the king, saying-Let the car go hence, dragged slowly, step by step. Obeying my will, do you two proceed in such a way that I may not feel any exhaustion.

verses.sanskrit: श्रमो मम यथा न स्यात्तथा मच्छंदचारिणौ । सुसुखं चैव वोढव्यो जनः सर्वश्च पश्यतु ॥३६॥
नोत्सार्याः पथिकाः केचित्तेभ्यो दास्ये वसुह्यहम् । ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च ये कामानर्थयिष्यन्ति मां पथि ॥३७॥
verses.english: I should be borne away pleasantly, and let all your people see this march that I make through their midst. No person that comes to me, as I proceed along the road, should be driven away. I shall distribute riches among all.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वान्दास्याम्यशेषेण धनं रत्नानि चैव हि । क्रियतां निखिलेनैतन्मा विचारय पार्थिव ॥३८॥
verses.english: To the Brahmanas who may approach me on the way, I shall grant their wishes and bestow upon all of the them gems and riches without stint.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा भृत्यांस्तथाऽब्रवीत् । यद्यद्ब्रूयान्मुनिस्तत्तत्सर्वं देयमशङ्कितैः ॥३९॥
verses.english: Let all this be done, O king, and do not entertain any scruples!-Hearing these words of the Rishi, the king called his servants and told them-Ye should without any fear, give away whatever the ascetic will command. Then profuse jewels and gems and beautiful women, and pairs of sheep, and coined and uncoined gold, and huge elephants resembling, hills or mountain summits, and all the ministers of the king, began to follow the Rishi as he was carried on that chariot.

verses.sanskrit: ततो रत्नन्यनेकानि स्त्रियो युग्यमजाविकम् । कृताकृतं च कनकं गजेन्द्राश्चाचलोपमाः ॥४०॥
अन्वगच्छन्त तमृषिं राजामात्याश्च सर्वशः । हाहाभूतं च तत्सर्वमासीन्नगरमार्तवत् ॥४१॥
तौ तीक्ष्णाग्रेण सहसा प्रतोदेन प्रतोदितौ । पृष्ठे विद्धौ कटे चैव निर्विकारौ तमूहतुः ॥४२॥
verses.english: Cries of Oh and Alas arose from every part of the city which was plunged in grief at that extraordinary spectacle. The Rishi struck the king and the queen suddenly with that goad having a sharp point. Though thus struck on the back and the cheeks, the royal pair still showed no sign of agitation. On the other hand they continued to carry the Rishi on as before.

verses.sanskrit: वेपमानौ निराहारौ पञ्चाशद्रात्रकर्शितौ । कथञ्चिदूहतुर्वीरौ दम्पती तं रथोत्तमम् ॥४३॥
verses.english: Trembling from head to foot, for no food had passed their lips for fifty nights, and exceedingly weak, the heroic pair somehow succeeded in dragging that excellent chariot.

verses.sanskrit: बहुशो भृशविद्धौ तौ स्रवन्तौ च क्षतोद्भवम् । ददृशाते महाराज पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ ॥४४॥
verses.english: Repeatedly and deeply cut by the goad, the royal pair became covered with blood. Indeed, O king, they then looked like a couple of Kinshuka trees in the flowering season.

verses.sanskrit: तौ दृष्ट्वा पौरवर्गस्तु भृशं शोकसमाकुलः । अभिशापभयत्रस्तो न च किञ्चिदुवाच ह ॥४५॥
verses.english: Seeing the plight to which their king and queen had been reduced, the citizens became afflicted with great grief. Filled with fear of the curse of the Rishi, they kept silent under their misery.

verses.sanskrit: द्वन्द्वशश्चाव्रुवन्सर्वे पश्यध्वं तपसो बलम् । क्रुद्धा अपि मुनिश्रेष्ठं वीक्षितुं नेह शक्नुमः ॥४६॥
verses.english: Collected in masses they said to each other-See the might of penances! Although all of us are angry, we are still unable to look at the Rishi.

verses.sanskrit: अहो भगवतो वीर्यं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । राज्ञश्चापि सभार्यस्य धैर्यं पश्यत यादृशम् ॥४७॥
verses.english: Great is the energy of the holy Rishi of purified soul! See also the endurance of the king and his royal spouse.

verses.sanskrit: श्रान्तावपि हि कृच्छ्रेण रथमेनं समूहतुः । न चैतयोर्विकारं वै ददर्श भृगुनन्दनः ॥४८॥
verses.english: Though exhausted with fatigue and hunger, they are still carrying the car! The son of Bhrigu, despite the misery he caused to Kushika and his queen, could see no sign of dissatisfaction or agitation in them.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच। ततः स निर्विकारौ तु दृष्ट्वा भृगुकुलोद्वहम् । वसु विश्राणयामास यथा वैश्रवणस्तथा ॥४९॥
verses.english: Bhishma said The perpetuator of Bhrigu's race, seeing the king and the queen totally unmoved, began to distribute wealth very largely as if he were a second Lord of Treasures.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रापि राजा प्रीतात्मा यथादिष्टमथाकरोत् । ततोऽस्य भगवान्प्रीतो बभूव मुनिसत्तमः ॥५०॥
verses.english: At this deed also, king Kushika showed no mark of dissatisfaction. He did as the Rishi ordered. Seeing all this, that illustrious and best of ascetics became pleased.

verses.sanskrit: अवतीर्य रथश्रेष्ठाद्दम्पती तौ मुमोच ह । विमोच्यं चैतौ विधिवत्ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह ॥५१॥
verses.english: Descending from that excellent car, he unharnessed the royal pair. Having freed them, he addressed them duty.

verses.sanskrit: स्निग्धगम्भीरया वाचा भार्गवः सुप्रसन्नया । ददानि वां वरं श्रेष्ठं तं ब्रूतामिति भारत ॥५२॥
verses.english: Indeed the son of Bhrigu, in a soft, deep, and delighted voice, saidI am ready to give an excellent boon to you both.

verses.sanskrit: सुकुमारौ च तौ विद्धौ कराभ्यां मुनिसत्तमः । पस्पर्शामृतकल्पाभ्यां स्नेहाद्भरतसत्तम ॥५३॥
verses.english: Delicate as they were, their bodies had been pierced with the goad. Moved by affection, that best of ascetics softly touched them with his hands, whose healing virtues resembled those of ambrosia itself, O chief of the Bharatas.

verses.sanskrit: अथाब्रवीन्नृपो वाक्यं श्रमो नास्त्यावयोरिह । विश्रान्तौ च प्रभावात्ते ऊचतुस्तौ तु भार्गवम् ॥५४॥
verses.english: Then the king answered Myself and my wife have felt no exhaustion Indeed, all their fatigue had been removed through the power of the Rishi, and hence it was that the king could say so to the Rishi.

verses.sanskrit: अथ तौ भगवान्प्राह प्रहृष्टश्च्यवनस्तदा । न वृथा व्याहृतं पूर्वं यन्मया तद्भविष्यति ॥५५॥
verses.english: Pleased with their conduct, the illustrious Chyavana said to them I have never before spoken falsehood; It must, therefore be as I have said.

verses.sanskrit: रमणीयः समुद्देशो गङ्गातीरमिदं शुभम् । किञ्चित्कालं व्रतपरो निवत्स्यामीह पार्थिव ॥५६॥
verses.english: This spot on the banks of Ganga is very charming and auspicious. I shall, observing a vow, live for a little while here, O king.

verses.sanskrit: गम्यतां स्वपुरं पुत्र विश्रान्तः पुनरेष्यसि । इहस्थं मां सभार्यस्त्वं द्रष्टासि श्वो नराधिप । न च मन्युस्त्वया कार्यः श्रेयस्ते समुपस्थितम् ॥५७॥
verses.english: Do you return to your city. You are exhausted! You shall come again. Tomorrow, O king, you shall returning with your wife, see me here.

verses.sanskrit: यत्कांक्षितं हृदिस्थं ते तत्सर्वं हि भविष्यति । इत्येवमुक्तः कुशिकः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ॥५८॥
verses.english: You should not give to anger or grief. The time is come when you shall reap a great reward! That which is coveted by you and which is in your heart will indeed be done.

verses.sanskrit: प्रोवाच मुनिशार्दूलमिदं वचनमर्थवत् । न मे मन्युर्महाभाग पूत्रौ स्वो भगवंस्त्वया ॥५९॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by the Rishi, king Kushika, with a pleased heart, replied to the Rishi in these pregnant words.

verses.sanskrit: संवृतौ यौवनस्थौ स्वो वपुष्मंतौ बलान्वितौ । प्रतोदेन व्रणा ये मे सभार्यस्य त्वया कृताः ॥६०॥
verses.english: I have entertained no anger or grief, O highly blessed one! We have been cleansed and sanctified by you, O holy one! We have once more become youthful. See our bodies have become greatly beautiful and possessed of great strength.

verses.sanskrit: तान्न पश्यामि गात्रेषु स्वस्थोऽस्मि सह भार्यया । इमां च देवीं पश्यामि वपुषाऽप्सरसोपमाम् ॥६१॥
verses.english: I do not any longer see those wounds that were caused by you on our bodies with your good! Verily, with my wife, I am in good health.

verses.sanskrit: श्रिया परमया युक्ता तथा दृष्टा पुरा मया । तव प्रसादसंवृत्तमिदं सर्वं महामुने ॥६२॥
verses.english: I see my goddess become as beautiful in body as an Apsara. Indeed, she is endued with as much beauty and splendour as she had ever been before.

verses.sanskrit: नैतच्चित्रं तु भगवंस्त्वयि सत्यपराक्रम । इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचैनं कुशिकं च्यवनस्तदा ॥६३॥
verses.english: All this, O great ascetic, is due to your favour, Indeed, there is nothing wonderful in all this, O holy Rishi of power ever unbaffled.

verses.sanskrit: आगच्छेथाः सभार्यश्च त्वमिहेति नराधिप । इत्युक्तः समनुज्ञातो राजर्षिरभिवाद्य तम् ॥६४॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by the king, Chyavana said to him – You shall, with your wife, return here tomorrow, O king.

verses.sanskrit: प्रययौ वपुषा युक्तो नगरं देवराजवत् । तत एनमुपाजग्मुरमात्याः सपुरोहिताः ॥६५॥
verses.english: With these words, the royal sage Kushika was sent away. Saluting the Rishi, the king, endued with a handsome body, returned to his capital like a second king of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit: बलस्था गणिकायुक्ताः सर्वाः प्रकृतयस्तथा । तैर्वृतः कुशिको राजा श्रिया परमया ज्वलन् ॥६६॥
verses.english: The counsellors then, with the priest, came out to welcome him. His troops also and the dancing women and all his subjects, did the same.

verses.sanskrit: प्रविवेश पुरं हृष्टः पूज्यमानोऽथ बंदिभिः । ततः प्रविश्य नगरं कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकीः क्रियाः । भुक्त्वा सभार्यो रजनीमुवास स महाद्युतिः ॥६७॥
verses.english: Each saw the other to be possessed of fresh youthfulness. All their sufferings and pains having ceased, they saw each other to resemble a celestial, Gifted with the splendour they had got as a boon from that foremost of Brahmanas, and possessed of exceedingly lovely features and beautiful forms, both of them passed a happy night in their bed.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु तौ नवमभिवीक्ष्य यौवनं परस्परं विगतरुजाविवामरौ । ननन्दतुः शयनगतौ वपुर्धरौ श्रिया युतौ द्विजवरदत्तया तदा ॥६७॥
verses.english: Each saw the other to be possessed of fresh youthfulness. All their sufferings and pains having ceased, they saw each other to resemble a celestial, Gifted with the splendour they had got as a boon from that foremost of Brahmanas, and possessed of exceedingly lovely features and beautiful forms, both of them passed a happy night in their bed.

verses.sanskrit: अथाप्यृषिर्भृगुकुलकीर्तिवर्धनस्तपोधनो वनमभिराममृद्धिमत् । मनीषया बहुविधरत्नभूषितं ससर्ज यन्न पुरि शतक्रतोरपि ॥६८॥
verses.english: In the interval spreader of the feats of Bhrigu's race, viz., the Rishi having penances for his wealth, converted by his Yogapower, that charming wood on the bank of Ganga into a retreat full of wealth of every kind and adorned with every variety of jewels and gems on account of which it excelled in beauty and splendour the very abode of the king of the celestials.
